clue.text: Something we all have in common

definitions.text: Something we all have in common

parts.words: Something we all have in common
parts.note: a thing held in common by everyone reads as a shared trait, but means land or goods owned by the community at large

explanation.surface: A remark on the shared traits of humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets owned by the state or community belong to everyone in common, so this is a cryptic description of communal ownership.

clue.text: Systematic assembly of parts in play, say, with a bit of text

parts.note: a play is an example of a theatrical production, hence 'say'
a line is a short piece of written text

explanation.surface: A drama is put together with a snatch of script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' suggests roles in the play, but here it means factory components.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory arrangement where workers add components in sequence is a systematic assembly of parts.

clue.text: Vehicle of half-crazy proposer

parts.note: the old song 'Daisy Bell' has a suitor who is 'half crazy' proposing on a machine 'built for two'

explanation.surface: Asking what transport a lovestruck suitor uses.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'Daisy, Daisy' has the line 'I'm half crazy all for the love of you' and ends with a two-seater cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer of 'Daisy Bell' proposes that they ride a tandem, a two-wheeled pedal vehicle.

clue.text: Surliness I shall moderate

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall, written without its apostrophe
to temper is to moderate or soften

explanation.surface: Someone promising to tone down their grumpiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad temper and surliness are both grumpy, irritable moods; synonym.

clue.text: Sends to prison stores

definitions.meaning: to lock someone up in jail
to put things somewhere safe for later

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both jailing a person and tidying goods into storage.

clue.text: Loosened bosses grip

indicators.note: loosened suggests the letters are freed and allowed to fall in a new order

explanation.surface: Employers are no longer so tight-fisted with their staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grip' seems the opposite of 'Loosened' in the surface, but as a verb it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When a thought grips you, it preoccupies your mind completely; synonym.

clue.text: It's a mistake to be led astray over gold

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written over another means it comes first

parts.note: to err is to stray from the right path
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Being lured off course by riches is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or blunder is simply a synonym for a mistake.

clue.text: A child of three allowed on an excursion

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed on another sits beneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion
let means allowed, as in 'let in'

explanation.surface: A three-year-old is permitted to join an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A child of three' reads as a toddler aged three, but means one of three born together.
explanation.definitionFit: One of three babies born at one birth is a child of three in the multiple-birth sense.

clue.text: The Deep South?

parts.note: the Deep South suggests the American states, but 'deep' is the sea, and the far south is the polar region

explanation.surface: A reference to the southern United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic term for the sea, and the waters around the South Pole are the southernmost sea.

clue.text: Big copper's embracing ex with kisses

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so one piece encloses the next

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the possessive 's giving an S
late means former, as an ex is

explanation.surface: A burly policeman hugs his former partner with kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is a formal or jocular word meaning to kiss; synonym.

clue.text: Check the key in, as a rule

indicators.note: in places the key inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Verifying the key is in place, as is usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like the idiom 'usually'; here 'rule' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period of their rule; synonym.

clue.text: Cryptic clue about northern relative

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled word wraps the letter for northern
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A puzzling hint concerning a family member from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' turns CLUE into UCLE, which goes about N.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: First class return to Southern Pacific country

indicators.note: to means added to the end of the word that follows

parts.note: austral means southern

indicators.note: return signals that the first-class letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, written here as the letters AI

explanation.surface: Coming back first class to the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns AI into IA, which is added to AUSTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This nation lies in the southwestern Pacific, so it is a Pacific country.

clue.text: He paints badly, so becomes an actor

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together poorly, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poor painter changes career to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespis was the first Greek actor, so his name gives a word for a performer on stage.

clue.text: Lyrical writer gets the twitch

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer of poems and tales
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A songwriter develops a nervous spasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lyrical writer' tempts as one phrase for a poet; 'writer' alone is POE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing has the qualities of verse; synonym.

clue.text: Insulting attack

definitions.meaning: an assault launched by an army

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for rude and a noun for a military assault.

clue.text: Conifers specially prepared for a court

indicators.note: specially prepared suggests the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Pine trees are readied for a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a royal court, but means a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic evidence is evidence prepared for use in a court of law.

clue.text: Processed heroin available at a price

indicators.note: processed means treated and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refined drugs are sold for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or tool for rent is available for a fee, so it is available at a price.

clue.text: He was bound to begin the show

definitions.text: He was bound to begin the show

parts.words: He was bound to begin the show
parts.note: bound means certain, but literally the escape artist was tied up with chains before each performance

explanation.surface: Someone was certain to open the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Houdini was the famous escapologist who began acts tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous escapologist was literally bound in chains at the start of his act.

clue.text: Papers thrown at union meeting

parts.note: suggests documents hurled at a trade union assembly, but the union is a wedding

explanation.surface: Documents hurled at a trade union assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper are thrown over a couple at a wedding, the union.

clue.text: It's most apt use is on a sailing vessel

definitions.text: It's most apt use is on a sailing vessel

indicators.note: use here means the words are applied in another order, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A remark about where something is best employed: aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a ship's mast section and the letters of 'most apt' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest section of a ship's mast is found only on a sailing vessel.

clue.text: I breathe fresh air in European peninsula

parts.note: to breathe is to live, to be

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying the clean air of southern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain and Portugal sit on the peninsula of that name in southwest Europe.

clue.text: It's hilarious, blowing up a huge ball

indicators.note: blowing up means exploding, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Inflating a giant ball is very funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laughable provokes laughter, so it is funny, hilarious.

clue.text: At heart, it's such a noisy capital

indicators.note: at heart means in the middle of the words that follow, so the letters are found there

explanation.surface: Remark about a loud capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Vietnam; example.

clue.text: No more old slang from Poona?

indicators.note: from here signals that the letters come from the place name, rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether an outdated slang term came from an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the term did not really come from Poona (it comes from soldiers' French 'il n'y en a plus').
explanation.definitionFit: This First World War soldiers' slang term meant finished or gone, so 'no more'.

clue.text: Scot returns service in Scotland

indicators.note: returns signals the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish name
RN is the Royal Navy, a military service

explanation.surface: A Scotsman goes back to military service in his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns IAN into NAI; NAIRN is a town in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: This town lies on the Moray Firth, so it is a place in Scotland.

clue.text: Its curate is about to take up a country living

indicators.note: about here means around or turned about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parish priest is about to move to a rural parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country living' suggests a church living, but means moving to the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate is to go to live in the countryside; synonym.

clue.text: Mathematician saw reactions in a new way

indicators.note: in a new way signals the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone observed responses in a fresh fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The scientist who formulated the laws of motion, including that every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: The English scientist was also a great mathematician, a co-inventor of calculus.
